Pre-Campaign · Monday May 11

One day of coordination,
then the drumbeat starts.

No public warm-up. The internal moves that have to happen before Tuesday's first PR — investor heads-up, partner amplification, embargoed press briefings — all land on Monday May 11. The goal is the right people aware and aligned the night before, not a week-long whisper that risks spoiling the launch. The work begins when the announcements are confirmed locked, not before.

Mon · May 11 · AM
Investor & board pre-brief emailOne-page heads-up to existing angels and the board: full campaign calendar, key milestones, what to amplify and when. Lands in their inbox before any public movement. Gives them ownership of the narrative — and the chance to start sharing on Tuesday morning, not Tuesday evening.
Mon · May 11 · AM
Customer & partner amplification heads-upDirect note to Saldo Bank, Payout Partner, and the partners locked into the first three weeks. Coordinated quotes, share-ready assets, embargoed PR copy, and a clear ask: amplify the day-of from your own channels. Saldo's comms team in particular needs the runway to coordinate their Tuesday morning post.
Mon · May 11 · PM
Embargoed press first-looksBriefings to 3–5 key Nordic fintech reporters (E24, Finansavisen, Shifter, Nordic9, Tech.eu) under embargo lifting at 8am CET Tuesday. The trade-off: they get the story 18 hours before publication. We get same-day coverage on the Tuesday PR drop instead of waiting a week.

— The Strategic Spine —

The red thread
connecting it all.

Three strategic pillars. Every press release, every use case, every social post laddering up to one of them — and through them, to the same destination: Celeri as the operational layer underneath frontline work.

→
— Pillar 01

Earned Wage Access
as the wedge

Real-time pay is how we get in the door. It drives positive employee engagement, lifts shift uptake, reduces absenteeism, and creates the moment of truth that opens up the rest of the relationship.

▲
— Pillar 02

Shadowing legacy systems,
then optimizing

We are not LLM wrappers. We are agentic, AI-native operational infrastructure that quietly sits behind PlanDay, accounting tools and payroll providers — then surfaces optimizations that compound into measurable employer ROI.

●
— Pillar 03

Platforms & partners
as our distribution

Banks, staffing apps, accounting suites, gig platforms, AI matching engines. Every partnership multiplies our reach into thousands of frontline workers — without us having to find them one by one.

Receipts. Four customers proving the thesis.

— Marketing Support · Use-Case Films —

Four customers.
Four films. One visual language.

Each use case earns a 30–60 second film, designed to live as the hero asset on celeri.com, the headline reel in pitch decks, and the most-shareable social cut. Below: the universal principles every Celeri film follows, then the per-customer brief.

01 · TONE

Documentary, not advertising

Real workers, real shifts, real moments. No re-enactments. No actors. If something feels staged, recut it. The audience can smell production from a mile away.

02 · STRUCTURE

Pain → Wedge → Outcome

Open with the operational problem (pain). Show Celeri quietly solving it (wedge). Close on a measurable, named outcome the customer can defend on camera (outcome).

03 · HERO MOMENT

One paycheck-landing shot

Every film must contain at least one shot of a worker seeing pay land on their phone. That moment is the campaign's emotional through-line. Capture it across multiple workers; pick the most authentic.

04 · BRAND

Quiet logo, loud silence

Celeri logo only at the end card, never overlaid on the work. Use Vesper Libre for any on-screen text. Brand red for hero stats. Acid green for the end-card logo lockup. Music: ambient and licensed; never pop.

Film 01 · Horeca

Agora

Hospitality · Norway · 45 seconds
Theme
"A day saved is a day earned." Show what one full day a week back means for a hospitality operator — not as an abstract stat, but as the operations manager actually getting their lunch break, leaving on time, taking a Friday off.
Setting
Agora's actual venue, mid-shift transition. Front-of-house and back-of-house. Shoot at golden hour for the dinner-rush opener and natural late afternoon light for the resolution scene. One shoot day; two-camera A-roll.
Beat-by-beat shot list
0:00–0:08
Wide of Agora at peak service. Energy, motion, controlled chaos. Title card: "BEFORE." Acid green underline.
0:08–0:18
Cut to the ops manager in her office, looking at PlanDay, on the phone, surrounded by paper. Voice-over (her own): "Used to be 8 to 8."
0:18–0:30
Quick cuts: Celeri dashboard mid-shift, AI-suggested swap, manager tapping approve, staff phones lighting up with confirmations. No narration. Just ambient sound.
0:30–0:38
Manager closing her laptop. Walking out the back door. Title card: "AFTER." Brand red.
0:38–0:45
Hero stat in Vesper Libre Black: "1 day saved per week." End card with Celeri logo lockup.
Required customer voice
Single line, Agora ops lead: "It's not that I work less. It's that I finally work on the right things." Voice-over only — no on-camera.
Film 02 · Logistics

Brightway

Staffing · Finland · 50 seconds
Theme
"From benefit to growth lever." Show how offering real-time pay didn't just attract more applicants — it attracted a better applicant pool, and that compositional shift grew Brightway's customer base.
Setting
Three locations: a Helsinki logistics hub at dawn (workers arriving), a Brightway operator's office (the applicant-volume dashboard), and a finished delivery route. Shoot bilingual title cards (English + Finnish).
Beat-by-beat shot list
0:00–0:10
Cold open: empty loading dock at 5:30am. Hold on the silence. One worker arrives. Title card: "The hardest job in staffing isn't the work." Pause. "It's filling the shift."
0:10–0:22
Brightway dashboard view: applicant graph rising. Voice-over from Brightway ops lead: "We turned on real-time pay. The applicants didn't just go up — they got better."
0:22–0:34
Cuts of multiple workers receiving pay on their phones — at the depot, in vehicles, at break. Authentic reactions. Diverse worker pool.
0:34–0:42
Brightway customer (logistics-provider lead) on camera, single line: "Their fill rate is the best in the market. That's why we use them." Bilingual subtitle.
0:42–0:50
Hero stat: "Real-time pay → applicant quality → operator value → revenue." Each step animates in. End card.
Required customer voice
Two voices: Brightway ops lead (voice-over) AND a logistics-provider customer (on-camera, ~8 seconds). The second voice is mandatory — it's what proves the "growth lever" claim.
Film 03 · Retail & Events

Comod

Influencer-driven staffing · Norway · 40 seconds
Theme
"Work that fits the life, not the other way around." Comod is repositioning shift-work — primarily in retail and live events — as something young people actually want to do. Workers build their own profiles, pick shifts that match their lifestyle, get paid in real time, treat the income as a spending-money lifestyle hack rather than a traditional job. Celeri sits quietly underneath, making real-time pay the texture of the experience. The film should feel like a TikTok native, not a corporate testimonial.
Setting
Real Comod work environments — retail floor pop-ups, event venues mid-load-in, festival activations, brand-experience setups. Shoot in natural light with a handheld feel — vertical-first. Workers should look like the actual Comod talent pool: 18–28, expressive, profile-aware, the kind of people building careers in fragments rather than nine-to-fives. Full colour throughout. Energy: editorial-meets-street, never staged.
Beat-by-beat shot list
0:00–0:10
Open on a young Comod worker scrolling shifts on their phone, casual setting (café, tram, bedroom). Voice-over (worker, audio only): "I don\'t do part-time jobs. I do shifts that fit my week."
0:10–0:22
Quick cuts: profile setup, shift accepted, retail floor or event activation in motion, the worker actually working — looking good while doing it. Voice-over continues: "Comod lets me build my own profile. I pick what I want. I get paid the same day."
0:22–0:32
Hero moment: pay landing on the worker\'s phone right after the shift ends. Hold on the screen. Cut to the worker spending it (coffee, concert ticket, train fare home). Voice-over: "That\'s the lifestyle hack."
0:32–0:40
End card: "Comod × Celeri. Real-time pay for the work that fits your life." Pilot data publishing H2 2026.
Required customer voice
Real Comod worker on voice-over throughout — not a CFO, not a founder. Cast someone who is genuinely active on the platform, ideally with a small social following so they can post the film themselves on the day. The voice should feel like a friend explaining a hack, not a brand explaining a value prop. End card line: "Real-time pay for the work that fits your life."
Film 04 · Live Events

Piknik i Parken

Festival · Norway · 60 seconds
Theme
"A wedge becomes a platform — inside AEG Presents Norway." The film tells the full Piknik arc: a festival (now part of AEG Presents Norway, the regional arm of one of the world\'s biggest live-entertainment groups) came to Celeri with a recruitment problem (declining young-applicant numbers), got earned wage access as the answer, and discovered — once the platform was deployed — that it could quietly run their entire workforce operation: paid staff, volunteers, scheduling, attendance, pay. End-to-end, without them having imagined it possible. The strategic subtext: this is also a working pilot inside AEG\'s global portfolio. The film should be confident about the wedge-to-platform thesis, and quietly confident about the audience watching.
Setting
The full Piknik i Parken site across all three festival days (June 2 onwards — actual festival runs late June). Shoot setup day, peak operational day, teardown day. The film must convey scale, energy, and that staff are real young Norwegians having a real summer.
Beat-by-beat shot list
0:00–0:12
Open on a young Norwegian flipping through her phone, applying for festival jobs. Cut to a Piknik ops desk: an applications graph trending DOWN over the past few summers. Title card: "Piknik came to Celeri with a recruitment problem."
0:12–0:24
Workers signing up, getting onboarded, shifts being planned. The applications graph reverses — climbing again. Voice-over (Festival Director): "We brought in earned wage access. Applications climbed almost immediately."
0:24–0:36
Mid-festival ops room. Celeri dashboard live: shift swaps, volunteer assignments, attendance tracking. Voice-over: "Then we realized — we could run the whole operation here. Paid staff, volunteers, scheduling, swaps, all of it." Cut tight: hands across keyboards, screens showing complex schedules turning simple.
0:36–0:48
Quick cuts of multiple workers — bartender, volunteer, security, food vendor, runner — all checked-in, all in motion, all visibly part of one system. The hero moment: a worker checking pay landing on her phone between shifts. Hold on her face. Music swells.
0:48–0:60
Pull back to a wide of festival at golden hour. Voice-over (AEG Presents Norway MD): "We couldn\'t have imagined doing it this way before. Now we can\'t imagine doing it any other way." Hero stat: "Recruitment wedge → full workforce layer. One platform." Final end card, two lines: "Piknik i Parken — part of AEG Presents Norway." Below it, smaller: "Global event-portfolio pilot, in plain sight."
Required customer voice
AEG Presents Norway MD (founder of Piknik i Parken) on-camera, single take, on-site. Three questions: "Why did you bring Celeri in?" (answer: the recruitment problem at Piknik) — "What surprised you?" (answer: that it ended up running the whole operation) — "What does this mean for the wider AEG Presents Norway portfolio?" (answer: kept careful and forward-looking; do NOT script an over-claim about other AEG markets). The closing line at 0:48 — "We couldn\'t have imagined doing it this way before. Now we can\'t imagine doing it any other way." — is the soundbite the entire film is built around. Get it on the first take, then again, then again. Pick the warmest one. AEG Presents Europe communications must approve the final cut before any publication.
